name: DELETE /api/routing-rules/:id - Retire a routing rule
description: Retires a routing rule by deactivating it. THIS IS A SOFT DELETE AND ALWAYS WILL BE: a routed lead holds routing_rule_id as a foreign key, so a hard delete would either violate that constraint or, with a cascade, erase the attribution that makes a past routing decision explainable. The question 'why did this lead go to Priya?' must stay answerable after the rule is retired, so the row is kept and only is_active flips to false. Answers 200 with a summary rather than a bodyless 204 (MUST-54), because the caller needs to know whether this call retired the rule or found it already retired, and because the resulting rule state is worth returning. IDEMPOTENT: retiring an already-retired rule answers 200 with already_inactive:true rather than failing, so a double-click or a retry is harmless. The retired rule still appears in GET /api/routing-rules (which returns all rules unless active=true is passed) but is excluded from routing decisions. This endpoint takes no request body; source_channel is documented in fieldEnums because the retired rule is RETURNED in the response and that field is enum-backed, so QA reading the API docs sees its valid values. QA: depends on register, login and a created rule.

transitions.notes: Sets is_active to false. The row is NOT removed, so leads that reference routing_rule_id keep their attribution.
A retirement is reversible — the row was never destroyed.

errorCases.when: the id path parameter is not a well-formed UUID
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
no rule exists with the supplied id
